Definition: % of Citrix virtual app or desktop session launch attempts that succeed without error, measured across all delivery groups and Delivery Controllers.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Launch success not tracked. Users report failures frequently. No visibility.
Level 2 - Developing: Launch success tracked manually. Rate below 90%. Failures investigated only after escalation.
Level 3 - Defined: Launch success monitored via Director. Rate between 90-97%. Alerts on failure spikes.
Level 4 - Managed: Rate above 97%. Automated alerting. Failure patterns analysed. Root cause analysis for recurring issues.
Level 5 - Optimized: More than 99% success rate. Predictive monitoring. Auto-recovery of failed VDAs. Real-time Director dashboards.

Definition: Total elapsed time from a user initiating a Citrix session to reaching a usable desktop or application, including authentication, profile load, and GPO processing.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Logon times not measured. Users frequently complain of slow logons. No baseline established.
Level 2 - Developing: Logon times occasionally measured. Average exceeds 120 seconds. No optimisation effort.
Level 3 - Defined: Logon time monitored. Average between 60-120 seconds. Profile and GPO optimisation in progress.
Level 4 - Managed: Average logon below 60 seconds. Profile solution optimised using FSLogix or UPM. GPOs streamlined.
Level 5 - Optimized: Average logon below 30 seconds. Fully optimised. Synthetic transaction monitoring. Proactive alerting on degradation.

Definition: The time in milliseconds for a round-trip of ICA protocol packets between the client and VDA, a primary indicator of perceived session responsiveness. Target is below 150ms.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: ICA RTT not monitored. User experience complaints not correlated with network metrics.
Level 2 - Developing: RTT monitored ad hoc. RTT often exceeds 300ms. No SLA. Users report poor performance.
Level 3 - Defined: RTT monitored via Director or Analytics. Average below 200ms for most users. Alerts configured.
Level 4 - Managed: Average RTT below 150ms. Alerts trigger network review. Branch optimisation applied.
Level 5 - Optimized: Average RTT below 100ms. HDX adaptive transport optimised. SD-WAN integrated. Per-user SLA reporting.

Definition: Frequency of ICA session reliability auto-reconnection events occurring due to network interruptions, measured per 1000 active sessions per day.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Session reliability events not tracked. Users experience frequent disconnections.
Level 2 - Developing: Events tracked reactively. More than 10 events per 1000 sessions per day. Root cause unknown.
Level 3 - Defined: Events tracked via Director. Between 5-10 per 1000 sessions per day. Network issues identified.
Level 4 - Managed: Fewer than 5 events per 1000 sessions per day. Network remediation is proactive. Trend reporting in place.
Level 5 - Optimized: Fewer than 1 event per 1000 sessions per day. Predictive network analytics. Zero disconnection SLA for critical users.

Definition: % of Virtual Delivery Agents that are successfully registered with a Delivery Controller and available to accept user sessions at any given time.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: VDA registration not monitored. Unregistered VDAs discovered only when users report failures.
Level 2 - Developing: Registration monitored manually. Rate below 90%. Unregistered VDAs not auto-remediated.
Level 3 - Defined: Registration rate tracked in Director. Above 93%. Alerts on unregistered VDAs.
Level 4 - Managed: Registration rate above 97%. Auto-remediation attempted on unregistered VDAs. Daily reporting.
Level 5 - Optimized: More than 99% registration rate. Automated self-healing. Root cause auto-diagnosed. Zero user impact.

Definition: % uptime of Citrix Delivery Controllers across all sites, which are the management and session brokering layer for the Citrix estate.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No monitoring of Delivery Controller health. Failures discovered by users.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic ping monitoring. Single Delivery Controller per site with no redundancy. Downtime exceeds 0.5%.
Level 3 - Defined: Redundant Delivery Controllers per site. Availability monitored. Targeting 99.9%.
Level 4 - Managed: 99.9% availability. Automated failover tested. Health checks integrated with ITSM.
Level 5 - Optimized: 99.99% availability. Active-active configuration. Auto-failover. Synthetic transactions validate health.

Definition: % uptime of Citrix StoreFront servers, which serve the web or application portal through which users launch virtual apps and desktops.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: StoreFront availability not monitored. Single StoreFront with no redundancy.
Level 2 - Developing: Storefront monitored via basic checks. Downtime events occur monthly. No redundancy.
Level 3 - Defined: Redundant StoreFront servers deployed. Load balanced. Availability above 99%.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 99.5% availability. Synthetic logon tests run every 5 minutes. Alerting integrated.
Level 5 - Optimized: 99.99% availability. Multi-site StoreFront with GSLB. Automated failover. Zero user-impacting outages.

Definition: % uptime of Citrix Netscaler devices, which external users use as a gateway to launch virtual apps and desktops.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Netscaler availability not monitored. Single Netscaler with no redundancy.
Level 2 - Developing: Netscaler monitored via basic checks. Downtime events occur monthly. No redundancy.
Level 3 - Defined: Redundant Netscalers deployed. Load balanced. Availability above 99%.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 99.5% availability. Synthetic logon tests run every 5 minutes. Alerting integrated.
Level 5 - Optimized: 99.99% availability. Automated failover with HA setup. Zero user-impacting outages.

Definition: Available capacity headroom for concurrent user sessions above the observed peak load, expressed as a % buffer above peak demand.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Session capacity unknown. Environment regularly hits capacity limits. Users unable to connect.
Level 2 - Developing: Capacity tracked manually. Headroom below 10% above peak. Load spikes cause failures.
Level 3 - Defined: Session capacity monitored. Between 10-20% headroom maintained. Monthly capacity reviews.
Level 4 - Managed: Between 20-30% headroom maintained. Automated scaling triggers. Capacity forecasting in place.
Level 5 - Optimized: More than 30% headroom. Auto-scaling via MCS or Citrix Autoscale responds to demand. Predictive scaling.

Parameter / KPI: VDA CPU and Memory Utilisation per Session
Definition: Average CPU and memory consumed per active Citrix session on each VDA, used to validate VM sizing and detect resource contention.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Per-session resource utilisation not tracked. VDA sizing not optimised. Performance complaints frequent.
Level 2 - Developing: Utilisation tracked at host level only. No per-session data. VDAs frequently exceed 85% CPU.
Level 3 - Defined: Per-session metrics collected via Director or monitoring tool. Sizing guidelines defined.
Level 4 - Managed: Per-session CPU below 30% and memory below 2GB on average. Right-sizing reviews quarterly.
Level 5 - Optimized: Automated right-sizing recommendations. Per-session SLAs enforced. Anomalous sessions auto-terminated.

Parameter / KPI: VDA OS and Citrix Version Compliance
Definition: % of Virtual Delivery Agents running an OS version and Citrix VDA software version within supported lifecycle and within the approved patch currency window.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: VDA versions not tracked. Mix of EOL OS and outdated Citrix versions in production.
Level 2 - Developing: Version inventory exists but more than 20% of VDAs on unsupported or EOL versions. No roadmap.
Level 3 - Defined: Inventory maintained. Patch currency tracked. Between 5-20% behind. Upgrade plan in place.
Level 4 - Managed: Less than 5% on unsupported versions. Patch pipeline automates VDA updates via MCS image refresh.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% on supported versions. Image refresh automated. Zero EOL VDAs. Compliance dashboards in real time.

Definition: % of privileged user, high-risk application, and regulated-environment Citrix sessions recorded via Citrix Session Recording for audit and forensic purposes.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No session recording. No audit trail of user activity within Citrix sessions.
Level 2 - Developing: Session recording deployed but used only for incident investigation. No formal policy.
Level 3 - Defined: Recording policy defined for privileged users. More than 60% of target sessions recorded.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 90% of defined high-risk sessions recorded. Recordings indexed and searchable.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% coverage for all defined policies. AI-based activity detection. Forensic-grade storage.

Definition: % of Citrix remote access connections subject to Endpoint Analysis scans validating device compliance such as AV status, OS patch level, and domain membership before granting session access.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No EPA configured. All devices can connect regardless of security posture.
Level 2 - Developing: EPA deployed but not enforced. Scan results not used to control access.
Level 3 - Defined: EPA enforced for external and remote connections. Non-compliant devices restricted to quarantine.
Level 4 - Managed: EPA enforced for all connections. Policies updated to match current compliance requirements.
Level 5 - Optimized: EPA enforced with adaptive access. Non-compliant devices auto-remediated or blocked. Logs feed SIEM.

Definition: Time taken to load a user profile including FSLogix container mount or UPM profile sync as part of the overall logon process. Target is below 15 seconds for the profile loading component.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Profile load time not measured. Profiles bloated and unmanaged. Logon storms common.
Level 2 - Developing: Profile load often exceeds 60 seconds. No size limits. Profiles stored on overloaded file servers.
Level 3 - Defined: Profile load between 15-60 seconds. FSLogix or UPM deployed. Basic size limits enforced.
Level 4 - Managed: Profile load below 15 seconds. FSLogix ODFC containers on high-performance storage.
Level 5 - Optimized: Profile load below 5 seconds. Containers on NVMe or all-flash storage. Pre-load technology. Zero profile corruption.

Definition: % of FSLogix profile or Office Container attach operations that succeed without error, and % of containers within defined size limits.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: FSLogix not deployed. Roaming profiles or no profiles in use. Frequent corruption.
Level 2 - Developing: FSLogix deployed but not monitored. Container attach failures occur daily. No size limits.
Level 3 - Defined: FSLogix health monitored. Attach success rate above 90%. Size alerts configured.
Level 4 - Managed: Attach success above 97%. Sizes within policy. Failed attaches auto-remediated.
Level 5 - Optimized: More than 99% attach success. Automated container health checks. Bloated containers auto-alerted. Zero data loss.

Definition: Age and patch state of the Citrix master image used to provision VDAs via MCS or PVS, measured by time since last update and patch coverage.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No golden image process. VDAs built manually. Images months out of date.
Level 2 - Developing: Golden image updated infrequently, more than 3 months old. Manual update process. Testing minimal.
Level 3 - Defined: Image updated monthly. Patches included. Basic functional testing before deployment.
Level 4 - Managed: Image updated with each patch cycle. Automated build pipeline. Smoke tests run pre-deployment.
Level 5 - Optimized: Image fully automated. CI/CD pipeline builds, patches, tests, and deploys images. Zero manual steps.

Definition: % of non-persistent VDA machines governed by Citrix Autoscale or equivalent power management policies, ensuring machines are drained and shut down during off-peak hours to reduce infrastructure costs.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No power management. All VDAs powered on 24/7. Significant resource and cost waste.
Level 2 - Developing: Power management partially configured. Many VDAs run overnight unnecessarily.
Level 3 - Defined: Autoscale configured for most delivery groups. Off-peak capacity reduced by more than 40%.
Level 4 - Managed: Autoscale optimised per delivery group schedule. Cost savings tracked and reported.
Level 5 - Optimized: Autoscale with dynamic scaling. ML-based demand prediction. Cost optimisation reported monthly.

Definition: SSL certificates are installed on the delivery controllers, storefront servers, FSLogix and Netscaler devices for secure communication.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No monitoring of SSL certificates expiry and expiry alerts not configured
Level 2 - Developing: Partial monitoring of SSL certificate expiry installed in the servers
Level 3 - Defined: Alerts configured through monitoring tool for 75% of the servers prior to the expiration date
Level 4 - Managed: Expiry dates are properly tracked through alerts and certificate renewal is done 30 days prior to the expiry date.
Level 5 - Optimized: Expiry dates are properly tracked through alerts for 100% of all servers and certificate renewal is done 30 days prior to the expiry date. All information documented and reported weekly.
